assumptions_note: All figures are indicative national averages used to start a conversation. Actual milk yield, prices and feed costs vary by breed, region and season; edit the inputs in AgriN to match your farm.

steps.title: Start with 1-2 cows (or buffaloes/goats) on your own fodder
steps.detail: Grow green fodder (Napier, sorghum, lucerne, azolla) on 10-15% of the land so feed cost stays low. Prefer local, hardy breeds; register with the local dairy cooperative for a guaranteed milk buyer.

steps.title: Set up a compost pit or vermicompost bed
steps.detail: Heap dung, urine-soaked bedding and crop residue in a shaded pit or brick tank; it turns into manure in 60-90 days (vermicompost in about 45).

steps.title: Add a small biogas plant
steps.detail: Dung yields cooking gas (saving LPG) and nutrient-rich slurry manure. 2-3 cows feed a 2 m3 household plant.

steps.title: Make Jeevamrut and Panchagavya from dung and urine
steps.detail: These fermented cow-based inputs feed soil biology and replace part of the chemical fertiliser bill.

steps.title: Add milk value-addition
steps.detail: Convert surplus milk to curd, ghee or paneer for 2-3x the price of raw milk; join a dairy cooperative or women's SHG.

steps.title: Diversify: poultry, goats, bees, fish, agroforestry
steps.detail: A mix of enterprises spreads risk when one crop or market fails. Bees lift pollination and honey income; trees on bunds give fodder, fruit and timber.

steps.title: Keep records and use insurance
steps.detail: Record milk, feed, and manure. Insure crops and livestock (PMFBY and livestock insurance in India) and keep a small emergency fund.

enterprises.name: Dairy (cow/buffalo)
enterprises.start_cost_note: Depends on breed; loans via KCC and Rashtriya Gokul Mission support in India.

enterprises.name: Vermicompost
enterprises.start_cost_note: Low cost: pits or beds under shade.

enterprises.name: Backyard poultry
enterprises.start_cost_note: Very low; local breeds are hardy.

enterprises.name: Beekeeping
enterprises.returns: Honey, wax, higher yields via pollination
